title: Ralph Neely: 1964 Consensus All-American Tackle at Oklahoma
question: Which Oklahoma tackle was a 1964 consensus All-American and later starred for the Dallas Cowboys?
answer: Ralph Neely, an offensive tackle who played at Oklahoma from 1962 to 1964, was a consensus All-American in 1964. He then spent 13 seasons with the Dallas Cowboys and played his last game in Super Bowl XII.
summary: Ralph Neely, Oklahoma tackle from 1962 to 1964, earned consensus All-America honors in 1964, then played 13 seasons for the Dallas Cowboys.
body: Ralph Neely arrived at Oklahoma as a lineman who would be remembered for his play along the offensive front. He suited up for the Sooners from 1962 through 1964, playing for Bud Wilkinson and then Gomer Jones. Sports Illustrated's Sooners coverage lists him as a two-time All-Big Eight selection and the Big Eight's top sophomore lineman in 1962.

His best-known college honor came in 1964, when he was a consensus All-American at tackle. That season Oklahoma finished 6-4-1 and drew a Gator Bowl invitation. The same coverage ranks Neely at the top of its list of former Sooner offensive linemen, a good measure of how highly OU fans regard him.

The pros wanted him badly. He was a second-round draft pick in 1964, and his rights ended up with Dallas, where he became a fixture of the Cowboys line. Over 13 seasons he started at right tackle early on and later moved to the left side. Reports on his career credit him with two Pro Bowls, four All-Pro selections and a place on the NFL's All-Decade Team for the 1960s.

Neely was part of Dallas teams that reached four Super Bowls, and he retired after the Cowboys beat Denver in Super Bowl XII. He died in January 2022 at age 78, and former teammates and Sooner fans remembered him as one of the best linemen to wear both the OU and Dallas colors.
